summary:
EV-O006-01 came back INCONCLUSIVE: A1 = 0.0206 against a 0.01 threshold, A2 = 0.143 K against 0.05 K, A4 = +inf against 0.5 K; A3 = 0.72 is met and kill criteria K1/K2 are not triggered. The run itself is valid: all 26 sanity checks pass and every evaluator provenance check is ok. I found no evidence that the L2 solver is wrong. There are two separate causes, each confirmed by a cheap local test.

(1) A1/A2. Every row over 0.05 K is in Muzychka Cases 1a or 2, which are single 10 mm plates. The frozen grid rule always puts 2 cells in each layer, whatever its thickness, so at level 2 the cells are 1.25 mm thick. Doubling only the through-thickness (z) cells cuts the Case 2 error from 0.143 to 0.040 K, and quadrupling them cuts it to 0.010 K. Doubling only the lateral cells changes nothing (0.150 K). Case 1a behaves the same way: 0.025 K with 16 z-cells even at 1 mm lateral cells. The solver converges to the validated reference at second order, with no bias above about 0.01 K.

(2) A4 = inf. All three divergent values are 'reference max' points that are bilinearly interpolated at a fixed (x, y) position. With each refinement, that point's relative position inside the interpolation stencil jumps around (ξ → (2ξ+½) mod 1). The interpolation error therefore has no C·h^p form, which the GCI assumes. Filling the production stencil with the exact field shows the FV error at those points is identical to the centroid's and falls by exactly 4.0 per level. With the interpolation part removed, the GCIs become 0.06–0.18 K instead of inf or 0.595 K. On the five generator layouts alone, A4 is 0.303 K. The pre-registration smoke run had already shown a divergent manufactured-case max point.

Primary class: model (the frozen grid rule's per-layer z count fails on thick layers). Secondary: an experimental defect in how A4 measures point values. The pre-registered decision for this outcome is 'same as fail' (switch to the scikit-fem fallback), and O006's only evaluation has been used, so the next step is the founder's.
root_cause: A1/A2: the frozen thermal grid rule sets Z_CELLS = 2 cells per layer regardless of thickness. On the 10 mm single-layer Muzychka Cases 1a and 2 this gives dz = 1.25 mm at level 2 and leaves 0.12–0.14 K of through-thickness discretisation error at the source means. The verified solver converges to the validated reference at second order in dz with no bias above about 0.01 K. A4 = +inf: the three-grid GCI is applied to bilinear interpolants at fixed off-lattice 'reference max' points. Their position inside the cell-centre stencil changes non-monotonically between levels (ξ → (2ξ+½) mod 1), so the interpolation error -½ξ(1-ξ)h²T'' has no C·h^p expansion. The estimator therefore reports 'divergent' even though the FV field there converges monotonically at order 2.
evidence: [F] Run E006-20261102T145940-2815 (commit bb0725f): all 26 sanity checks pass, energy balance max 1.5e-7, Picard 2.9e-5 K, F5 0.233 <= 0.25 K. Evaluator provenance checks all ok, so the run is valid.

[F] Every row with |err| > 0.05 K is in case2 or case1a. Top three: case2 s2.mean +1.374/+0.458/+0.143 K, case1a s2.mean +0.124 K, case2 s3.mean +0.114 K. Case 1b, Case 3, the N-layer DBC case and the manufactured case meet A1/A2 (max 0.026 K).

[F] Test 1 (t1_case2_refinement.py, reproduces rows.json exactly): Case 2 s2.mean error is +0.1431 at frozen L2, +0.0397 with z doubled, +0.0101 with z quadrupled, and +0.1495 with lateral doubled. Case 1a at L0 lateral with z refined to L3: +0.025 K. Lateral-only doubling: +1.508 K.
[F] The cell-sum source mean is less accurate than the interpolant mean (+0.160 vs +0.143 K), so the mean measurement is not the cause.

[F] Test 2 (t2_interp_stencil.py; exact field reproduces T_ref to within 4e-8 K): nlayer d1's FV column-centre error is +0.7530/+0.1885/+0.0472 at the centroid and +0.7535/+0.1887/+0.0473 at the max (ratio 4.00). The interpolation error at the max is -0.748/-0.110/-0.052, with stencil coordinate tx 0.747 -> 0.995 -> 0.489.
[F] Corrected GCIs (A4 rule on f_L - e_int): d1.max inf -> 0.177, d4.max inf -> 0.161, mms die_max inf -> 0.061, mms die_centroid 0.595 -> 0.0625, mms overhang 0.201 -> 0.0068.
[F] Max GCI on the five generator layouts alone is 0.303 K. Over all values except the four interpolation-affected ones it is 0.393 K (case2 s2.mean).
[F] The pre-registration smoke dev rows already had one divergent manufactured value and A4 = inf (research/notes/o006-e006-design.md section 4).

[F] N-layer DBC case at L0: refining z alone takes d2.centroid from +0.084 to -0.247 K; refining laterally alone takes it to +0.285 K. At L2 the FV column-centre error is about +0.047 K and the bilinear peak under-estimate is about -0.045 K, so the small A2 errors there are partly a systematic, stable cancellation.

Commands: t1 small/all/zsplit case1a/nlsplit nlayer_dbc all exit 0. t2 first attempt failed with a SyntaxError in my script, then exit 0 after the fix. ruff check exit 0. mfos gate --fast exit 0 ('all gates passed'). sysctl and ps were refused by the sandbox. Peak RSS of my jobs was 2.97 GB.

alternative_explanations.explanation: H2 implementation bias in the solver (flux assignment, T_c + q dz/2k reconstruction, linear solve)
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Refine until the error should vanish. Refuted: error falls 3.6x then 3.9x under z-doubling, to 0.010 K.
Independent scikit-fem check, and whether L2 converges to the series. Refuted: case2_vs_skfem 0.0011 K with scikit-fem's own GCI 0.0046 K, and the L2 converges to the series.

alternative_explanations.explanation: H4 the interpolant mean over the source pulls in values from outside the source edge
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Compare with the cell-sum mean. Refuted: the cell-sum mean is worse (+0.160 vs +0.143 K).

alternative_explanations.explanation: H5 lateral source-edge singularity, with edge grading inactive on thick plates (s_edge = 20 mm)
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Lateral-only refinement. Refuted as dominant: +0.1431 -> +0.1495 K.

alternative_explanations.explanation: G2 the FV field does not converge near the hot spot
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Column-centre error via exact-field stencil decomposition. Refuted: same error as the centroid, ratio 4.00.

alternative_explanations.explanation: G3 Picard/CG iteration noise drives the non-monotone A4 sequences
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: Step sizes vs the 1e-3 K floor, and smoothness at neighbouring points. Refuted: steps 0.005-0.08 K, Picard 2.9e-5 K, nlayer has constant k, the centroid 0.15 mm away is clean.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Label alternative: call A1/A2 'experimental', because Cases 1a/2 (10 mm plates) lie outside the DBC regime the decision concerns
alternative_explanations.how_to_discriminate: A judgement, not a test. The hypothesis explicitly includes Cases 1a/2 on the frozen rule, so I label it model. A founder could reasonably weigh it the other way.

discriminating_tests: Case 2 z-only vs lateral-only refinement at frozen level 2 (run: z-dominated, confirmed)
Case 1a z-split at lateral L0 (run: z-dominated, confirmed)
Exact-field substitution into the production SurfaceField stencil at the nlayer/MMS points (run: the interpolation stencil explains every A4 offender)
N-layer DBC z-split at L0 (run: z and lateral errors have opposite signs and similar size)
Not run (needs about 46 GB): Case 1a with z doubled at level-2 lateral resolution, to confirm the z-mechanism at the registered level
Not run: scikit-fem Case 2 with dz <= 0.3 mm as a third method on the binding rows
recommended_actions: Founder decision memo. O006's single evaluation is used, and the pre-registered inconclusive branch is 'same as fail' (scikit-fem fallback). Present (a) the pre-registered fallback under a new experiment id and (b) a model change: a re-frozen grid rule whose through-thickness cell size is bounded in absolute terms rather than per layer, tested under a new experiment id with a fresh sealed seed. State that no implementation defect was found.

For any successor experiment (new id): do not apply a three-grid GCI to bilinear values at fixed off-lattice points. Evaluate at grid lines that persist under bisection (ξ = ½), or compare column-centre values against the reference at those centres. Add a sanity check that reports stencil coordinates per level.

Before O003 relies on meta['solver_tol']: count divergent/oscillatory Tj-max sequences on dev layouts. Tj max is a discrete maximum and samples the true maximum through the same ξ-orbit; all 34 layout values here were fast/monotone.

Founder flag: hypothesis (c) bounds the GCI 'on those layouts', but A4's description also includes reference-case values (layouts alone: 0.303 K). A2's 'corner-free' rationale does not anticipate through-thickness under-resolution on 10 mm plates. No threshold change is recommended; this is for the founder to weigh.
Do not re-evaluate O006 on the same run or data after any change; use fresh sealed seeds only.
